historical_claims.anchor: Davis and Kahan announce a convention at the start of their paper: some of their results are vacuous when certain norms occurring in them fail to exist, and they will not mention this at each statement.
historical_claims.source_locator: Section 1, paper-wide convention after the setting

historical_claims.anchor: Davis and Kahan's Lemma 5.1 says: for each index j, the j-th approximation number of K times Omega t converges to the j-th approximation number of K.
Robert Schatten developed normed operator ideals in his 1950 monograph A Theory of Cross-Spaces, and the systematic theory of symmetrically normed ideals was later developed by Gohberg and Krein.
historical_claims.source_locator: Secondary account; primary: Schatten, A Theory of Cross-Spaces (Princeton, 1950); Gohberg and Krein, Translations of Mathematical Monographs 18 (AMS, 1969). Neither primary has a verified link in this catalog.

historical_claims.anchor: Davis and Kahan define the singular values of a bounded operator through the same min-max formula used for matrices, and note that for noncompact operators the language of spectral multiplicity may be more appropriate.

related_resources.reason: Trace-class operators, the trace norm, and why the identity on an infinite-dimensional space is not trace class.
Hilbert-Schmidt operators and the Hilbert-Schmidt norm, including diagonal examples like diag(1/n).
Two-sided operator ideals in the algebra of bounded operators.
Notes on trace-class and Hilbert-Schmidt operators and their ideal properties.
The best low-rank approximation result that identifies approximation numbers with singular values for compact operators.
